- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) or volatile, model underestimates; add 5–10% to forecast, especially near end of horizon.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 2–5% on day after spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; dampen forecast by 3–5% if sentiment swings >0.4 in 3-day window.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.6 → -0.3 → +0.6), model fails to adjust; apply 2–4% downward correction on next forecast.
